articles.title: DNSFilter makes its DNS threat protection available to OEM partners
articles.summary: DNSFilter has launched an OEM program allowing ISPs, device manufacturers, and security firms to integrate its protective DNS, domain analysis, and VPN/firewall solutions into their own platforms. This move aims to broaden the reach of their threat-blocking capabilities through third-party product bundling.

articles.title: Attestiv DeepScan combines AI and forensic analysis for file validation
articles.summary: Attestiv has launched DeepScan, an AI-powered platform designed to automatically validate the authenticity of files like photos, documents, and media within business workflows. The tool integrates forensic analysis to help organizations verify trust in customer-submitted content and combat deepfake threats.

articles.title: UNK_MassTraction Exploits Roundcube Flaws Against US, Canadian Universities
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor UNK_MassTraction is exploiting vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail to compromise research email servers at universities in the U.S. and Canada. The attackers are successfully stealing user sessions to gain unauthorized access to sensitive academic data.

articles.title: GitHub 'Verified' Commits Can Be Rewritten Into New Hashes Without Breaking Signatures
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that Git commit hashes can be rewritten while maintaining a valid signature, allowing attackers to create deceptive commits that GitHub erroneously marks as 'Verified'. This vulnerability undermines the integrity of code review processes by allowing for the generation of valid-looking but technically distinct commits.

articles.title: The Verification Step Is the New ATO Battleground in 2026
articles.summary: As traditional credential stuffing becomes less effective due to the adoption of passkeys, attackers are shifting their focus to exploiting the identity verification process to facilitate account takeovers.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot Refuses Harmful Requests in Chat, Then Writes Them in Code
articles.summary: Researchers found that AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot can be manipulated into generating malicious code by breaking dangerous requests into smaller, innocuous steps within the code editor. This highlights a security bypass vulnerability in current LLM-based development tools.

articles.title: Telegram-Hosted RedWing Malware Lets Anyone Rent Android Spyware Tools
articles.summary: The RedWing Android banking trojan is being distributed as a subscription-based malware-as-a-service model via Telegram, showing potential ties to the Oblivion malware family and Russian threat actors. It lowers the barrier to entry for cybercriminals by providing comprehensive tutorials and documentation for its spyware capabilities.

articles.title: Crusoe brings serverless fine-tuning to AI model development
articles.summary: Crusoe has introduced serverless fine-tuning and self-serve deployment capabilities to its Intelligence Foundry platform, streamlining the development and production of custom AI models. These tools aim to reduce infrastructure management overhead for data scientists and ML engineers working with open-weight models.

articles.title: Automox MCP Server adds visual reviews and AI-driven patch policy creation
articles.summary: Automox has released version 2.2 of its MCP Server, introducing interactive visual review tools and AI-powered patch policy creation to enhance governance in endpoint operations. This update aims to move beyond simple natural-language interaction by providing IT teams with better oversight and actionable context for automated patch management.

articles.title: China-Linked UAT-7810 Expands ORB Network With New LONGLEASH Malware
articles.summary: Chinese threat actor UAT-7810 is expanding its LapDogs ORB network by compromising internet-facing devices with new bespoke malware named LONGLEASH. This activity highlights the ongoing development of advanced infrastructure by persistent actors.

articles.title: Thousands of malicious AI skills found capable of stealing data, running malware
articles.summary: The ESET H1 2026 Threat Report identified over 25,000 suspicious AI skills capable of stealing user data and executing malware. These malicious extensions significantly expand the attack surface for AI agents by abusing their permissions to perform unauthorized tasks.

articles.title: Found fast, fixed slow: The gap the AI clearinghouse must close
articles.summary: The government's AI clearinghouse needs to prioritize rapid vulnerability remediation over mere discovery to be effective. Relying solely on scanning without integrated patching processes risks rendering the initiative ineffective.

articles.title: ScienceLogic adds geographic service visibility to Skylar One
articles.summary: ScienceLogic has released the 'Kyoto' update for its Skylar One observability platform, introducing new features for geographic service visibility and improved hybrid IT infrastructure management. This update focuses on enhancing AI workload monitoring and platform scalability for enterprise environments.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Adobe ColdFusion, Joomlack Page Builder, Langflow, and JoomShaper SP Page Builder flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include multiple security flaws found in Adobe ColdFusion, Joomlack Page Builder, Langflow, and JoomShaper SP Page Builder. Federal agencies are mandated to remediate these specific vulnerabilities to mitigate active exploitation risks.

articles.title: Codenotary launches AI security platform that learns from AI agent behavior
articles.summary: Codenotary has launched AgentMon 3, an AI security platform that utilizes adaptive runtime policies to monitor and learn from AI agent behavior within organizational workflows. The tool is now available on the AWS Marketplace to simplify enterprise deployment.

articles.title: CISA Deploys Anthropic’s Mythos AI to Hunt Vulnerabilities in U.S. Government Code
articles.summary: CISA has begun utilizing Anthropic’s Mythos AI to proactively scan federal government code repositories for security vulnerabilities. This initiative aims to identify and remediate potential flaws before they can be exploited by foreign intelligence services or cybercriminals.

articles.title: Claude Cowork turns your phone into a remote control for AI work
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Cowork, an AI agent capable of executing multi-step tasks across various applications that persist in the background even when devices are offline. This tool allows users to manage complex workflows remotely through mobile and web interfaces.

articles.title: 15-Year-Old GhostLock Flaw Enables Root and Container Escape on Most Linux Distros
articles.summary: GhostLock (CVE-2026-43499) is a 15-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unprivileged local users to gain root access and escape containers. The flaw affects nearly all mainstream distributions since 2011 and requires immediate patching.

articles.title: Orbia CISO Miranda Ritchie on building security into sustainable infrastructure
articles.summary: Orbia CISO Miranda Ritchie discusses the critical intersection of cybersecurity, safety, and sustainable infrastructure within industrial control systems. She emphasizes embedding security into project lifecycles to mitigate risks to personnel and the environment caused by legacy hardware and distributed operational technology.

articles.title: CISA Adds 4 Actively Exploited Adobe, Joomla, and Langflow Flaws to KEV
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include four actively exploited security flaws discovered in Adobe ColdFusion, Joomla, and Langflow. These additions require federal agencies to remediate the vulnerabilities within a specified timeframe to mitigate active threats.

articles.title: 20 open-source cybersecurity tools to keep your team ready for anything
articles.summary: This article highlights 20 open-source cybersecurity tools designed to assist security teams with vulnerability research, application testing, and AI-specific infrastructure protection. It emphasizes the growing need for tools that secure AI systems against emerging threats like exposed endpoints.

articles.title: macOS is becoming a proving ground for AI agents
articles.summary: The emergence of AI agents capable of autonomous operation on macOS systems presents new security challenges regarding automated workflows and potential threat actor abuse. These agents simulate human interaction, which could be exploited to perform unauthorized tasks or automate malicious processes.

articles.title: How to implement a continuous offensive security testing program
articles.summary: This article discusses the shift from static penetration testing to continuous offensive security programs, addressing the need for constant monitoring to keep pace with evolving network environments and emerging threats.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are pulling in different directions
articles.summary: The increasing use of autonomous AI agents in operational workflows creates a potential security gap due to unpredictable behavioral drift that eludes traditional monitoring. An analysis of hiring trends at OpenAI and Anthropic suggests that these companies are prioritizing different developmental paths for agentic AI.

articles.title: Why Unity Remains the Most Popular Engine for Mobile Games
articles.summary: This article discusses the technical advantages and industry-standard features that make the Unity game engine a preferred choice for mobile game development. It focuses on development efficiency and scalability rather than security risks.

articles.title: Vidar Stealer Unmasked: Code Signing Abuse, Go Loaders and File Inflation
articles.summary: The Vidar Stealer campaign employs advanced evasion techniques, including code signing abuse and a custom Go-based loader that utilizes DLL sideloading to infect systems. This combination of a loader-as-a-service framework and file inflation represents a sophisticated evolution in threat actor methodology.

articles.title: Spain arrests suspected hacker linked to Russian hacktivist campaign
articles.summary: Spanish authorities have arrested a suspected hacker allegedly involved in cyberattacks orchestrated by the Russian hacktivist groups Cyber Army of Russia Reborn and NoName. The individual is currently being investigated for their role in these hostile campaigns.

articles.title: Critical Gitea Docker Bug Under Active Exploitation Exposes Repositories and Secrets
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20896) in Gitea Docker images that allows unauthorized access to sensitive repositories and secrets. Users are urged to upgrade to version 1.26.3 or later to remediate the flaw.

articles.title: Windows is watching: Anti-piracy tool fingers Scattered Spider suspect
articles.summary: Microsoft's Windows GDID telemetry tool has been utilized to identify a suspect associated with the Scattered Spider cybercriminal group. This case highlights how pervasive OS-level tracking can be leveraged by law enforcement to trace malicious online activity.

articles.title: Deepfake CSAM lawsuit against xAI, Grok expands
articles.summary: A lawsuit involving the generation of non-consensual deepfake sexual images of minors using xAI's Grok and Stability AI has expanded to include additional victims and defendants. The case highlights the legal and ethical challenges surrounding generative AI tools and child safety.

articles.title: GitHub AI agent leaks private repos when asked nicely
articles.summary: A security vulnerability nicknamed GitLost in a GitHub AI agent allows unauthorized users to access private repositories through simple prompt injection techniques. Currently, there is no official fix or documentation addressing the exploit.

articles.title: Spanish Police Arrest Man Linked to CARR, Z-Pentest, and NoName057(16)
articles.summary: Spanish police, in collaboration with the FBI, arrested a suspect in Palencia for providing coordination and financial support to pro-Russian hacking groups including CARR, Z-Pentest, and NoName057(16). The individual faces charges related to terrorism and cyberattacks.

articles.title: CAI cloud worm gives competitors' malware the boot, then steals secrets and mines for coin
articles.summary: A new cloud-based worm dubbed CAI is infecting environments not only to steal credentials and mine cryptocurrency but also to actively remove competing malware from the compromised systems. This behavior highlights an emerging trend of malicious actors sabotaging one another to maximize their control over infected infrastructure.

articles.title: RedWing MaaS Packages Android Bank Fraud as a Telegram Rental Service
articles.summary: The RedWing Android banking malware is being distributed as a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) subscription on Telegram, enabling low-skill threat actors to steal banking credentials and intercept 2FA codes. Researchers believe this operation is a new variant of the previously identified Oblivion malware.

articles.title: 7 Arrested Over World’s Top Anime Piracy Site HiAnime
articles.summary: Vietnamese authorities, in collaboration with US law enforcement and the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment, arrested seven individuals linked to the operation of the major anime piracy platform HiAnime, which generated $12.85 million in advertising revenue.

articles.title: Rogue Agent Flaw Could Have Let Attackers Hijack Google Dialogflow CX Chatbots
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in Google Dialogflow CX allowed attackers with restricted access to hijack other chatbots within the same cloud project. This flaw enabled unauthorized access to sensitive user data and the ability to manipulate chatbot responses for phishing purposes.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Texas app law requiring age verification to take effect
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has permitted the Texas App Store Accountability Act to take effect, allowing the state to enforce age verification requirements on app stores. This decision denies an emergency request to stay the law while ongoing legal challenges proceed in lower courts.

articles.title: Predatorgate snoopfest victims launch €8M sueball at spyware maker
articles.summary: Victims of the 'Predator' spyware have initiated an €8 million lawsuit against the spyware developer in Greece. This legal action coincides with increased pressure from human rights organizations for the EU to implement stricter regulations against spyware abuse.

articles.title: Britain plans to build autonomous AI 'Cyber Shield' to defend nation
articles.summary: The British government is developing an autonomous 'Cyber Shield' to combat large-scale, machine-speed cyber threats identified by the National Cyber Security Centre. This initiative aims to enhance national defense by enabling automated detection and rapid response to sophisticated digital attacks.

articles.title: DEBULL Tooling Abuses Microsoft Device-Code Flow to Target M365 Accounts
articles.summary: The DEBULL phishing campaign exploits the legitimate Microsoft 365 device-code authentication flow by using social engineering lures to hijack user accounts. By bypassing traditional fake login pages, attackers trick victims into authorizing malicious device access directly through Microsoft's own interface.

articles.title: Major Japanese telco says cyberattack exposed 12 million emails
articles.summary: A major Japanese telecommunications company reported a cyberattack that exposed 12 million emails across five of its internet service providers. The breach compromised systems managing customer accounts, webmail services, and email storage.

articles.title: Public GitHub Issue Could Trick GitHub Agentic Workflows Into Leaking Private Repo Data
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a vulnerability where malicious actors can manipulate GitHub Agentic Workflows via public issues to exfiltrate data from an organization's private repositories. The attack requires no authentication or prior access, exploiting overly permissive agent configurations.

articles.title: Barracuda adds PAM and identity protection with Evo Security acquisition
articles.summary: Barracuda Networks has acquired Evo Security to integrate privileged access management and advanced identity protection capabilities into its BarracudaONE platform. This strategic move aims to provide a unified identity security architecture in response to the growing demand for comprehensive IAM solutions.

articles.title: CyberProof Agentic MXDR Service brings AI agents to managed detection and response
articles.summary: CyberProof has launched an Agentic MXDR service that utilizes AI agents to automate and integrate various security operations while maintaining human-governed oversight. The service aims to replace manual workflows in threat intelligence, hunting, and monitoring with an expert-validated AI system.

articles.title: Picus Autonomous Exposure Validation Platform validates real-world CVE exploitability
articles.summary: Picus Security has introduced an Autonomous Exposure Validation Platform designed to help organizations rapidly assess their vulnerability to real-world CVE exploits. The tool aims to bridge the gap between vulnerability disclosure and the ability to verify if security controls can effectively mitigate emerging threats.

articles.title: Court Filing Reveals Windows Device ID Helped FBI Trace Alleged Scattered Spider Hacker
articles.summary: U.S. prosecutors linked a 19-year-old alleged Scattered Spider hacker to a retail intrusion by tracking a persistent Windows device ID from Microsoft records to the suspect's accounts. The case highlights how hardware-level identifiers can be critical in deanonymizing cybercriminals.

articles.title: Writer AI Flaw Could Let Agent Previews Leak Session Tokens Across Tenants
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a critical session isolation flaw in the Writer AI platform, codenamed WriteOut, which allowed for cross-tenant unauthorized access by leaking session tokens. The vulnerability has since been patched by the vendor.

articles.title: UK cyber pledge draws only a handful of top firms despite ministerial appeal
articles.summary: A UK government initiative to boost corporate cybersecurity engagement has received low participation from major companies, despite being backed by high-profile firms like the London Stock Exchange and Marks & Spencer. The initiative follows significant recent cyber incidents that have impacted major businesses.

articles.title: GitLost: GitHub’s AI Agent Tricked Into Leaking Private Repository Data
articles.summary: Noma Labs identified a prompt injection vulnerability called GitLost that allowed unauthorized access to private GitHub repository data by exploiting the platform's AI agent and insufficient guardrails. This flaw demonstrates a significant security risk where manipulated public interactions can bypass access controls for sensitive information.

articles.title: Enterprise AI still smarting from leaping before looking
articles.summary: Enterprises are experiencing a high frequency of security incidents and vulnerabilities as a result of rapidly adopting artificial intelligence without adequate security considerations. A majority of organizations surveyed report issues directly stemming from their AI deployments.

articles.title: Commvault measures cyber recovery readiness with AI attack simulations
articles.summary: Commvault has launched 'Commvault Minutes to Recovery,' a cyber resilience simulation tool that utilizes AI to help organizations test their incident response and recovery capabilities against modern attack scenarios. The initiative highlights the critical need for rapid recovery, noting that the window for exploitation has shrunk to just 29 minutes.

articles.title: Attackers exploit critical Adobe ColdFusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-48282)
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion (CVE-2026-48282) shortly after technical analysis was published. Honeypot sensors detected exploitation attempts just two days after Adobe released the patch.

articles.title: What Changes When Your Software Supply Chain Includes AI Writing Your Code?
articles.summary: The integration of AI into software development pipelines introduces new security complexities, shifting the traditional supply chain focus beyond open-source dependencies to include risks associated with AI-generated code.

articles.title: Fake IT bods on Microsoft Teams coax workers into installing malware
articles.summary: Attackers are impersonating IT helpdesk staff on Microsoft Teams to trick employees into granting remote access and installing the EtherRAT trojan. This social engineering campaign exploits trust to facilitate unauthorized system access and malware deployment.

articles.title: Radware updates Agentic AI Protection with AI governance and compliance capabilities
articles.summary: Radware has enhanced its Agentic AI Protection solution to include new governance, compliance reporting, and security features for enterprise AI agents. These updates aim to help organizations meet global AI standards while securing environments that utilize third-party tools like Anthropic Claude Code.

articles.title: 4 Best Email Security Solutions to Keep Employee Inboxes Safe
articles.summary: This article provides a comparative review of top email security solutions, highlighting essential features like AI-based threat detection and phishing protection for organizational use.

articles.title: Spain collars alleged pro-Russia hacktivist after FBI tip-off
articles.summary: Spanish authorities arrested a man in Palencia for his suspected involvement in several pro-Russian hacktivist groups and for assisting a Ukrainian hacker in fleeing to Russia. The operation was facilitated by a tip-off from the FBI.

articles.title: Government's cyber pledge lands 60 signatories, including M&S and, somehow, Capita
articles.summary: The UK government has secured 60 corporate signatories for a new cyber hygiene pledge, featuring major retailers and Capita despite the latter's recent history of high-profile data breaches. The initiative aims to standardize security practices across the private sector through voluntary commitments.

articles.title: Hidden Tenda Router Backdoor Grants Admin Access, No Patch Available
articles.summary: CERT/CC has issued an alert regarding an unpatched authentication backdoor in multiple Tenda router models that allows attackers to gain full administrative access. There is currently no patch available to remediate this vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-11405.

articles.title: Suspected China-Aligned Hackers Exploit Roundcube Flaws Against Universities
articles.summary: Suspected China-aligned threat actors are exploiting critical vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail software to target U.S. and Canadian university departments. The campaign focuses on siphoning credentials by leveraging security flaws like CVE-2024-42009.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese espionage group used a Roundcube exploit chain to burrow into universities
articles.summary: A suspected Chinese espionage group is actively exploiting a chain of vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail to target university physics and engineering departments. Researchers warn that the campaign remains ongoing and poses a significant risk to academic institutions.

articles.title: AI-Generated Malware Powers New Armored Likho APT Campaign
articles.summary: The newly identified APT group Armored Likho is targeting government and infrastructure sectors in Russia, Kazakhstan, and Brazil using AI-generated malware and the BusySnake Stealer. The campaign exhibits a dual focus on both state-sponsored espionage and financial theft.

articles.title: Januscape: 16-Year-Old Linux KVM Bug Enables Cloud VM Escape Attacks
articles.summary: A 16-year-old use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux KVM hypervisor, dubbed Januscape, allows guest virtual machines to corrupt host kernel memory and potentially perform escape attacks. The flaw impacts both Intel and AMD systems.

articles.title: CERT/CC Warns of Hidden Admin Backdoor in Tenda Router Firmware
articles.summary: CERT/CC has issued an advisory regarding an undocumented authentication backdoor in Tenda router firmware that allows attackers to bypass password verification. This vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-11405, grants unauthorized administrative access to the web management interface of affected devices.

articles.title: Researchers make the case for a cybersecurity AI scientist
articles.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences are proposing a 'Cybersecurity AI Scientist' to automate security research, aiming to move beyond manual experimentation and address the scarcity of human expertise. This initiative seeks to apply autonomous AI agents to scientific discovery, mirroring their emerging success in practical penetration testing and vulnerability analysis.

articles.title: Review: Building Machine Learning Systems with a Feature Store
articles.summary: This article reviews Jim Dowling's book on building machine learning systems using feature stores, focusing on transitioning models from static datasets to real-time production environments. It highlights practical strategies for deploying robust, data-driven machine learning infrastructure.

articles.title: Your company already adopted AI and nobody is governing access
articles.summary: The rapid and unmonitored adoption of AI tools in the workplace is creating significant security risks, including unauthorized OAuth access and inherited permissions that lack corporate governance. CTO Antoine Berton warns that these shadow AI integrations expand the enterprise attack surface beyond current IT oversight.

articles.title: BeyondTrust Patches Critical Auth Bypass Flaws in Remote Support and PRA
articles.summary: BeyondTrust has released critical security patches for Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access to mitigate authentication bypass vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated attackers to gain control of affected devices.

articles.title: Apple Container: Open-source tool for Linux containers on the Mac
articles.summary: Apple has released an open-source tool called Container that allows developers to run Linux containers on Apple silicon Macs using individual, lightweight virtual machines. The tool is compatible with standard OCI images, enabling seamless integration with existing container registries.

articles.title: Microsoft wants to keep your AI agents from going rogue
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to provide a policy-driven security layer that restricts AI agent behavior and prevents them from performing unauthorized actions. This new tool simplifies the implementation of isolation controls for developers by enforcing runtime constraints on Windows and WSL.

articles.title: Power shortages could slow AI data center expansion
articles.summary: AI data center expansion is increasingly constrained by power shortages and infrastructure limitations, making electricity access a primary factor in project development. This operational bottleneck is impacting how quickly new AI capacity can be deployed globally.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: July 7, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security lists current job openings for cybersecurity professionals, including roles in application security and analysis for companies like Gett and Cynet Security.

articles.title: FBI and Spanish Police Arrest Alleged Cyber Army of Russia Reborn Member
articles.summary: The FBI and Spanish authorities have arrested an alleged member of the pro-Russia hacktivist group Cyber Army of Russia Reborn. This action reflects ongoing international collaboration to disrupt state-aligned cyber threat actors.

articles.title: Canadian spy agency reports hacking three criminal groups in 2025
articles.summary: Canada's Communications Security Establishment conducted offensive cyber operations against three distinct criminal organizations in 2025, including a ransomware-as-a-service gang. These actions represent a targeted disruption of illicit activities by a national intelligence agency.

articles.title: Attackers vote themselves $20 million in BONK cryptocurrency
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a governance mechanism in BonkDAO to fraudulently approve a proposal that transferred $20 million worth of BONK cryptocurrency to their wallets. This incident highlights a significant vulnerability in decentralized governance structures.

articles.title: Adobe ColdFusion flaw CVE-2026-48282 now exploited in the wild
articles.summary: A critical path traversal vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion, tracked as CVE-2026-48282, is being actively exploited in the wild to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw affects versions 2025.9, 2023.20, and earlier.

articles.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Use New Cavern C2 Framework to Target Israeli Organizations
articles.summary: An Iranian state-affiliated hacking group is utilizing a newly discovered modular C2 framework called Cavern to target Israeli IT and government sectors. The activity, tracked by Check Point Research, highlights evolving tactics used by the Ministry of Intelligence and Security to conduct targeted espionage.

articles.title: Major medical device manufacturer notifies nearly 4 million of breach
articles.summary: A major medical device manufacturer suffered a data breach affecting nearly 4 million individuals, resulting in the unauthorized access of sensitive data such as Social Security numbers and health information. Although the company reported no evidence of data exposure on the public internet, the incident remains a significant compromise of protected personal health information.

articles.title: US Army websites defaced with pro-Kurdish sentiments, insults to Trump
articles.summary: Two US Army websites were compromised via 404 hijacking to display pro-Kurdish messages and insults directed at the former president. The sites were subsequently taken offline by officials for investigation.

articles.title: 16-Year-Old Linux KVM Flaw Lets Guest VMs Escape to Host on Intel and AMD x86 Systems
articles.summary: A 16-year-old use-after-free vulnerability, dubbed 'Januscape' (CVE-2026-53359), in the Linux KVM hypervisor allows guest virtual machines to compromise the host kernel on Intel and AMD systems. The flaw resides in the shared shadow MMU code and is capable of causing host system panics.

articles.title: EU urged to act after Pegasus infects phone of spyware inquiry MEP
articles.summary: EU officials and campaigners are calling for immediate regulatory action following the discovery of Pegasus spyware on the device of a member of the European Parliament. The incident highlights ongoing security concerns regarding surveillance technology and underscores the need to implement recommendations from the PEGA Committee.

articles.title: Japanese teen arrested over cyberattack that disrupted anime streaming service
articles.summary: A Japanese teenager was arrested for exploiting a vulnerability in an anime streaming platform to perform unauthorized cancellations of over 46,000 user subscriptions. The incident highlights the impact of service-specific flaws on business operations and user account integrity.

articles.title: Threat Actors Probe Gitea Docker Flaw CVE-2026-20896 13 Days After Disclosure
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical Gitea Docker vulnerability, CVE-2026-20896, which allows unauthenticated attackers to gain elevated access. The exploit attempts were detected just 13 days after the vulnerability's initial disclosure.

articles.title: Sysdig clocks first documented case of agentic ransomware
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified the first documented instance of an AI-driven agentic ransomware attack, which enabled attackers to accelerate their operations and reduce the complexity of the exploit. This marks a notable evolution in how threat actors utilize autonomous AI agents to conduct malicious campaigns.

articles.title: From Image-to-3D to AI Agents: How AI 3D Generation Operates in 2026
articles.summary: This article explores the technical advancements in AI-driven 3D generation tools that convert text, images, and video into 3D models for various creative industries. It focuses on the capabilities of Meshy AI rather than cybersecurity threats.

articles.title: Criminal IP integrates threat intelligence with OpenCTI for automated indicator enrichment
articles.summary: Criminal IP has integrated its threat intelligence services with the OpenCTI platform, allowing security teams to automatically enrich and structure infrastructure data like IP addresses, domains, and URLs. This integration enables enhanced threat visualization and improved prioritization of indicators within the OpenCTI knowledge graph.

articles.title: Ukrainian media outlets now among 'priority targets' for Russian hackers
articles.summary: Ukrainian security officials report an escalation in Russian cyberattacks specifically targeting the nation's media organizations. Two previously undisclosed attacks highlight a shifting trend in which media outlets are now considered priority targets for state-sponsored threat actors.

articles.title: LTM’s BlueVerse RightLogic combines AI risk assessment with cyber remediation planning
articles.summary: LTM has introduced BlueVerse RightLogic, a cybersecurity framework that integrates AI-driven risk assessment with remediation planning to help enterprises manage exposure as they adopt new AI technologies.

articles.title: OpenSSH 10.4 arrives with security fixes and a post-quantum signature option
articles.summary: OpenSSH version 10.4 has been released, addressing eight security vulnerabilities and introducing support for post-quantum signature schemes. The update includes patches for issues discovered by the Swival Security Scanner, including a flaw in sftp.

articles.title: Hidden Web Prompts Trick AI Agents Into Sending Money
articles.summary: Researchers have identified active campaigns using indirect prompt injection to manipulate AI agents into executing unauthorized financial transactions. This vulnerability leverages hidden instructions on malicious websites to deceive autonomous workflows into trusting fake sites and initiating payments.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Proxy Botnets, Browser Ransomware, AI Agent Tricks, Fake PoC Malware and More
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape highlights a surge in attacks leveraging mundane infrastructure, such as home streaming devices and untrustworthy software dependencies, to facilitate botnet and ransomware campaigns. The recurring theme is the exploitation of inherent trust in ordinary systems, ranging from browser permissions to AI agent instructions.

articles.title: ClickFix Scams Abuse Google, Cloudflare Checks to Deliver 7 Malware Families
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging fake Google and Cloudflare browser verification pages, known as ClickFix, to trick users into executing malicious scripts that install various malware families. This campaign utilizes a shared infrastructure to deliver at least seven types of malware, including StealC and NetSupport.

articles.title: Brit supermarket giant triples down on facial recog to nab shoplifters
articles.summary: A major British supermarket chain is expanding its use of facial recognition technology to an additional 150 stores by the end of the year to combat shoplifting. This expansion has drawn criticism regarding privacy concerns and surveillance practices.

articles.title: Insignary Closes SBOM Accuracy Gap With Binary-Level Clarity for Regulatory Risk
articles.summary: Insignary has introduced binary-level analysis technology to improve the accuracy of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) reporting, addressing key regulatory compliance requirements. This solution helps organizations identify hidden security risks within software components to ensure better adherence to industry standards.

articles.title: How to Evaluate an AI SOC Platform in 2026: 6 Capabilities That Separate Leaders from Bolt-On AI solutions
articles.summary: The article provides a framework for evaluating AI-driven Security Operations Center (SOC) platforms, distinguishing between superficial 'bolt-on' AI assistants and advanced autonomous agent platforms. It aims to help organizations select solutions that provide meaningful operational improvements over legacy SIEM-based tools.

articles.title: Suspected China-Nexus Hackers Use Fake Indian Tax Filing Utility to Deploy DcRAT
articles.summary: Suspected China-linked threat actors are targeting Indian taxpayers with spear-phishing emails containing a fake tax utility that deploys the DcRAT malware to steal sensitive data. The campaign, identified as Operation DragonReturn, specifically aims to compromise financial professionals and corporate entities.

articles.title: Moody Bible Institute breach leaves 2.3M accounts needing salvation, says cyber expert
articles.summary: Moody Bible Institute confirmed a cyberattack resulting in the leak of personal data for 2.3 million accounts, with the threat actor ShinyHunters exposing names, addresses, and dates of birth.

articles.title: AI Can Forge Documents in Minutes – “Looks Right” Is No Longer Enough
articles.summary: Generative AI is enabling the rapid creation of sophisticated fraudulent documents, necessitating stricter verification protocols for file integrity and provenance. Security teams must move beyond visual inspection to automated validation methods to combat this evolving threat.

articles.title: Seven Bugs in FatFs Put IoT and Embedded Devices at Risk
articles.summary: Researchers at runZero have identified seven vulnerabilities in the FatFs filesystem library that could lead to memory corruption, system crashes, or potential data leaks in IoT and embedded devices. These flaws are triggered by processing specially crafted storage media.

articles.title: Secure Unix ancestor KSOS did type safety before Rust made it cool
articles.summary: Source code for the KSOS operating system, a Unix ancestor designed for high security and type safety, has been recovered after nearly 40 years. The project highlights early industry efforts to enforce memory safety through language design long before modern languages like Rust popularized the concept.

articles.title: Finding vulnerabilities was never the hard part
articles.summary: The rapid increase in AI-generated vulnerability discovery is overwhelming organizations, making it difficult to prioritize and manage significant security risks. The industry faces a challenge in distinguishing critical threats from noise at scale.

articles.title: New TrojPix Attack Leaks Data From Air-Gapped Systems via Video Cable Emissions
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered 'TrojPix,' a technique that exfiltrates data from air-gapped systems by modulating video cable electromagnetic emissions. The method requires prior malware infection on the target machine to manipulate pixel patterns for data transmission.

articles.title: Bad Epoll Flaw Gives Attackers Root Access on Linux and Android
articles.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability named Bad Epoll (CVE-2026-46242) allows local, unprivileged attackers to gain full root access on Linux systems and Android devices. The flaw, which evaded AI detection, requires immediate patching.

articles.title: New Java-Based QuimaRAT MaaS Built to Run on Windows, Linux, and macOS
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified QuimaRAT, a cross-platform Java-based remote access trojan offered as a malware-as-a-service (MaaS) that targets Windows, Linux, and macOS systems. The malware is currently being sold on subscription tiers ranging from $150 to $1,200.

articles.title: Opera GX Flaw Let Malicious Sites Auto-Install Mods to Steal Data From Visited Pages
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in the Opera GX browser allowed malicious websites to silently install unauthorized extensions to exfiltrate user data. The flaw has since been patched by Opera.

articles.title: SkillCloak Lets Malicious AI Agent Skills Evade Static Scanners with Self-Extracting Packing
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that a technique called SkillCloak uses self-extracting packing to help malicious AI coding agent add-ons evade detection by static security scanners. The study highlights a significant vulnerability in current security tools, which failed to detect the obfuscated malware in over 90% of tests.

articles.title: How to prioritize AI agent security by business impact
articles.summary: This article outlines a framework for prioritizing AI agent security by assessing business impact following an incident involving unauthorized access to a finance application. It highlights the risks posed by improper lifecycle management of OAuth grants for autonomous agents.

articles.title: Securing the inbox: Where identity, brand and security meet
articles.summary: Red Sift and GlobalSign have partnered to streamline the setup of DMARC, BIMI, and Verified Mark Certificates into a single package to simplify email brand authentication. This integration reduces the complexity and time required for organizations to verify their sender identity.

articles.title: Omnigent: Open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness
articles.summary: Omnigent is an open-source framework designed to unify diverse AI coding agents, addressing governance, credential management, and cost oversight challenges for development teams. It acts as a meta-harness to standardize operations across fragmented AI development tools.

articles.title: Product showcase: Is that text a scam? Malwarebytes Mobile Security can help you find out
articles.summary: Malwarebytes has released an updated mobile security application that integrates scam prevention, privacy protection, and identity monitoring across multiple operating systems. The tool aims to help users identify fraudulent text messages and improve their overall device security posture.

articles.title: Flipper Zero firmware development gets a fresh set of community rules
articles.summary: Flipper Devices has resumed active maintenance of the Flipper Zero firmware, implementing a new set of community guidelines for code contributions and feature requests. This move addresses recent concerns regarding the project's development inactivity.

articles.title: OAuth, guest accounts, and weak MFA drive SaaS risk
articles.summary: The over-provisioning and poor management of guest accounts, combined with insecure OAuth configurations and weak MFA, are creating significant security risks within SaaS environments. These overlooked access paths now account for the majority of SaaS identities, expanding the corporate attack surface.

articles.title: The future of payment fraud could be automated
articles.summary: Criminal groups are increasingly utilizing organized operations and agentic AI to automate payment fraud stages, such as credential theft and password cracking. As a result, consumers are prioritizing enhanced fraud protection when selecting financial service providers.

articles.title: New ClamAV security patch closes seven scanner bugs dating back two decades
articles.summary: Cisco Talos has released security patches for ClamAV versions 1.5.3 and 1.4.5 to address seven vulnerabilities, including long-standing flaws in executable file parsing.

articles.title: Medtronic Notifies 3.8 Million After ShinyHunters Data Breach
articles.summary: Medtronic has notified over 3.8 million individuals that their personal and medical data was compromised following a cyberattack by the ShinyHunters extortion group on its corporate IT systems.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 104
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware research, covering topics such as hijacked npm packages using VSCode for credential theft, CI/CD pipeline automation for Sigma rules, and the evolution of the StegoAd campaign.

articles.title: MFA-optional banks leave safe doors (and accounts) wide open for thieves to pillage
articles.summary: Financial institutions are exposing client accounts to unauthorized access by failing to mandate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). This prioritization of user convenience over security creates significant vulnerabilities that threat actors can exploit.

articles.title: Week in review: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited, Oracle EBS Payments flaw under attack
articles.summary: Recent cybersecurity reports highlight the active exploitation of SimpleHelp and Oracle EBS Payments vulnerabilities, alongside concerns regarding the rapid, insecure integration of AI features into enterprise software.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 584 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This Security Affairs newsletter highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including a $1 million ransom payment by a U.S. government agency and a FBI report on developer tool compromises by TeamPCP.

articles.title: U.S. Government Agency Paid $1M to Data Extortion Group Kairos
articles.summary: A U.S. government agency paid a $1 million ransom to the data extortion group Kairos following a security incident. The payment was confirmed via leaked negotiation transcripts and blockchain analysis detailed in a new Ransom-ISAC case study.

articles.title: U.S. Government Entity Paid Kairos $1 Million in Data-Theft Extortion Case
articles.summary: A U.S. government entity paid $1 million in extortion fees to a group known as Kairos to prevent the release of stolen data. Investigations suggest Kairos may be an extortion-only actor rather than a traditional ransomware gang, as there was no evidence of system encryption.

articles.title: The Lean Expansion Playbook AI Startups Are Using to Build Global Teams
articles.summary: This article discusses the operational strategies used by AI startups to scale globally by leveraging remote hiring, employer of record partners, and efficient management systems. It focuses on business growth and resource optimization rather than cybersecurity threats.

articles.title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors are actively distributing 108 malicious packages and extensions across multiple platforms as part of the ongoing PolinRider campaign. The attackers are compromising maintainer accounts to infect software supply chains.

articles.title: Confidential computing's core trust mechanism is broken. The fix may not exist
articles.summary: A fundamental vulnerability in Attested TLS compromises the core trust mechanism of confidential computing by preventing secure verification of endpoint identities. Researchers suggest that a definitive fix for this architectural flaw may not be feasible.

articles.title: FBI: TeamPCP Compromised Dev Tools to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a FLASH alert warning that the threat group TeamPCP is compromising developer tools and security software to exfiltrate cloud credentials and deploy malware. This campaign involves large-scale supply chain attacks aimed at both data theft and victim extortion.

articles.title: FBI: TeamPCP Compromised Dev Tools to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.summary: The FBI issued a FLASH alert regarding the criminal group TeamPCP, which compromised widely-used developer tools to steal cloud credentials and distribute malware. The group utilizes these compromised tools to gain unauthorized access to victim environments for extortion purposes.

articles.title: Unpatched Flaws Disclosed in Filesystem Bundled Into Millions of Embedded Devices
articles.summary: Security firm runZero discovered seven unpatched vulnerabilities in FatFs, a widely used filesystem library integrated into millions of embedded devices such as drones, cameras, and industrial controllers. These flaws pose a significant supply chain risk due to the library's ubiquity in hardware firmware.

articles.title: Pegasus Used Against MEP Investigating Pegasus, Citizen Lab Finds
articles.summary: Former MEP Stelios Kouloglou was targeted and repeatedly infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware while actively investigating the tool's use. This discovery highlights the ongoing misuse of advanced surveillance technology against political figures and oversight bodies.

articles.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Domains as Google Disrupts 2M Device Proxy Network
articles.summary: The FBI and Google have disrupted the NetNut proxy network by seizing domains linked to a scheme that hijacked 2 million smart TVs and streaming devices. This operation successfully dismantled a global infrastructure used to facilitate cybercriminal activity.

articles.title: New "Bad Epoll" Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Unprivileged Users Gain Root, Hits Android
articles.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability named 'Bad Epoll' (CVE-2026-46242) enables unprivileged users to achieve root access across desktop, server, and Android platforms. A patch has been released to address this flaw, which was identified in a kernel region recently highlighted by AI-driven analysis.

articles.title: New Avalon Malware Framework Packs CrownX Ransomware Capabilities
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new modular malware framework called Avalon, which utilizes multi-stage phishing to deploy diverse capabilities including credential theft, lateral movement, and ransomware execution. Its ability to bypass traditional security controls poses a significant risk to organizational environments.

articles.title: North Korea-Linked npm Packages Mimic Rollup Polyfills to Steal Developer Secrets
articles.summary: North Korean-linked threat actors are distributing malicious npm packages that masquerade as legitimate Rollup polyfill tools to exfiltrate developer data and gain remote access. The packages mimic the metadata of the authentic 'rollup-plugin-polyfill-node' library to deceive developers.

articles.title: AdaptHealth says attackers sweet-talked their way into cloud systems and stole patient data
articles.summary: AdaptHealth experienced a data breach after threat actors used social engineering against a third-party contractor to gain unauthorized access to cloud systems containing patient information and credentials. The incident resulted in the compromise of sensitive health data and insurance billing passwords.

articles.title: Armored Likho Targets Government Agencies, Power Sector with BusySnake Stealer
articles.summary: A newly identified threat actor dubbed Armored Likho is targeting government agencies and the energy sector in Russia, Brazil, and Kazakhstan using the BusySnake stealer for both espionage and financial gain.

articles.title: New PamStealer Malware Targets macOS Users via Fake Maccy Clipboard App
articles.summary: A new malware strain called PamStealer is targeting macOS users by masquerading as the legitimate Maccy clipboard utility to steal sensitive credentials and browser data. It poses a significant threat by exfiltrating passwords and clipboard contents from compromised systems.

articles.title: NetNut cracked as Google and FBI target 2 million-device botnet
articles.summary: Google and the FBI have dismantled a massive 2 million-device botnet infrastructure operated by NetNut, raising concerns that other residential proxy services may share similar compromised network vulnerabilities.

articles.title: JADEPUFFER: First End-to-End AI-Driven Ransomware Operation
articles.summary: Sysdig researchers have identified JADEPUFFER, the first documented ransomware operation conducted entirely by an AI agent using an LLM to perform end-to-end attack steps. This development marks a significant shift in threat actor capabilities, as the agent successfully navigated the environment and encrypted data without human intervention.

articles.title: European Parliament Member Investigating Spyware Was Hacked With Pegasus
articles.summary: Former MEP Stelios Kouloglou was repeatedly targeted with Pegasus spyware while serving on a committee investigating the abuse of commercial surveillance tools. Forensic evidence confirms his device was compromised, highlighting a direct attack on a European official tasked with oversight.

articles.title: The Anatomy of a Shadow AI Supply-Chain Breach: Lessons from the 2026 Vercel Incident
articles.summary: The 2026 Vercel incident occurred after an employee utilized an unvetted AI tool, allowing attackers to exploit it as a trusted gateway to access systems, exfiltrate data, and demand a $2 million ransom.

articles.title: Law enforcememt operation disrupted Malicious Residential Proxy Networks NetNut
articles.summary: Google and the FBI successfully disrupted NetNut, a massive residential proxy network exploited by cybercriminals to obfuscate their activities using compromised home devices.

articles.title: PamStealer Uses Fake Maccy Sites and PAM Checks to Steal Mac Login Passwords
articles.summary: PamStealer is a newly discovered macOS information stealer disguised as the clipboard manager Maccy that uses malicious PAM configuration checks to compromise user login credentials. The malware is distributed via fake websites as a malicious AppleScript file.

articles.title: Government and Healthcare Are the Weakest Links in Global Email Security
articles.summary: A study by Comparitech reveals that government and healthcare sectors have significant email security vulnerabilities due to widespread failure to implement standard authentication protocols like SPF, DMARC, DKIM, and MTA-STS. This oversight leaves these critical sectors highly susceptible to phishing attacks.

articles.title: Intezer helps SOC teams automate custom security tasks
articles.summary: Intezer has launched Custom Agents, enabling security operations teams to build and deploy personalized AI agents within its platform to automate triage and investigation tasks. This initiative aims to address the scalability challenges of managing modern security threats by shifting from manual processes to AI-supervised automation.

articles.title: User swore hacker called General Failure had invaded his PC
articles.summary: A user erroneously believed their computer had been compromised by a hacker named 'General Failure', likely misinterpreting a standard system error message. The incident highlights the confusion between technical error codes and actual security threats.

articles.title: Non-interactive SSH attacks dominate after login
articles.summary: Research using eleven honeypots reveals that the majority of post-login SSH attacks are automated and non-interactive rather than manual, human-led intrusions. This indicates a shift toward scripted malicious activity following initial server access.

articles.title: Geopolitical cyber threats are turning HR into a security front line
articles.summary: Geopolitical tensions are expanding the threat landscape, forcing organizations to treat departments like HR as primary targets for new, non-traditional adversaries. Security teams are encouraged to widen their threat models to account for these evolving global risks.

articles.title: Someone infected a spyware probe overseer with spyware
articles.summary: A member of the European Parliament's PEGA committee, which investigates spyware abuse, was targeted and infected twice by NSO Group's Pegasus spyware. This incident highlights the significant risks faced by individuals overseeing surveillance technology oversight.

articles.title: Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it
articles.summary: Stelios Kouloglou, a former member of the European Parliament committee investigating commercial spyware, was confirmed to have been infected with Pegasus spyware twice during his tenure. This incident highlights the targeted use of advanced surveillance tools against high-profile political figures involved in cybersecurity oversight.

articles.title: Organizations struggle to prioritize known cyber risks
articles.summary: Organizations are finding it difficult to effectively prioritize known cyber risks due to fragmented data across disconnected security tools and systems. Despite an abundance of risk information, the lack of a unified exposure view hinders comprehensive threat management.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: July 3, 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights recent cybersecurity product releases, specifically focusing on Digi International's new AI-powered network diagnostics agent, DANI. The agent is integrated into the Digi Remote Manager platform to streamline network operations and device management.

articles.title: Dev says Google warned him about account hijack – then charged him $11,000 anyway
articles.summary: A developer reported that Google notified him of a potential account hijack attempt, yet simultaneously allowed unauthorized access that resulted in an $11,000 charge on his account. The incident highlights a critical failure in Google's internal coordination between security alerting and billing protection systems.

articles.title: Startup sues Palo Alto Networks' Koi Security, saying an AI-hallucinated report falsely linked it to Chinese espionage
articles.summary: Startup MeetingTV has filed a lawsuit against Palo Alto Networks' Koi Security, alleging that an AI-generated threat intelligence report falsely accused the company of participating in Chinese espionage. The legal action seeks to compel the disclosure of the underlying evidence for these claims.

articles.title: How We Added WebAuthn to a Browser-Based RDP Client
articles.summary: The article details the technical implementation of WebAuthn redirection within a browser-based RDP client, enabling secure hardware-based authentication for remote sessions. This innovation enhances security by extending FIDO2/WebAuthn support to non-Windows RDP environments.

articles.title: VMware Licensing Changes and Their Impact on Infrastructure Modernization
articles.summary: VMware's shift to subscription-based licensing is forcing organizations to reassess their infrastructure and cloud strategies to maintain operational efficiency and AI readiness. This transition requires enterprises to perform a strategic evaluation of costs and architecture to mitigate potential risks to their modernization efforts.

articles.title: Launch of UK's National Cyber Action Plan delayed amid Labour leadership crisis
articles.summary: The release of the UK's National Cyber Action Plan has been delayed due to the ongoing leadership crisis within the Labour Party. The postponement pushes back the strategic publication originally scheduled for Monday.

articles.title: Google Disrupts NetNut Residential Proxy Network Spanning 2 Million Home Devices
articles.summary: Google, in collaboration with the FBI and other partners, successfully disrupted the NetNut residential proxy network by reducing its usable pool of millions of compromised home devices. The operation targeted the infrastructure used to facilitate illicit traffic relays through residential internet connections.

articles.title: Ransomware Groups Turn to Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD, and Supply Chain Credentials
articles.summary: Anubis ransomware operators are leveraging the Citrix Bleed 2 vulnerability for initial access, while utilizing legitimate RMM tools and credential harvesting for lateral movement. The campaign highlights a growing reliance on supply chain credentials and 'bring your own vulnerable driver' techniques to facilitate malicious operations.

articles.title: Smooth AI criminal drives 'first' end-to-end agentic ransomware attack
articles.summary: Researchers have identified the first fully autonomous, agentic ransomware attack driven by AI, demonstrating that malicious LLMs can now conduct end-to-end extortion campaigns without human intervention. The findings suggest that paying ransoms remains futile, as AI-driven agents cannot be relied upon to return stolen data.

articles.title: Europe Confirms Record €4.1B Penalty Against Google for Android Practices
articles.summary: The European Union's top court has upheld a record €4.1 billion fine against Google for leveraging Android's market dominance through anti-competitive licensing practices.

articles.title: Supreme Court decision threatens EU-US data transfer agreement
articles.summary: Privacy activist Max Schrems plans to challenge the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework in court, potentially disrupting the legal mechanism for transferring personal data between the two regions.

articles.title: FortiBleed Credential Theft Connected to INC and Lynx Ransomware
articles.summary: The FortiBleed credential theft campaign has been linked to the INC and Lynx ransomware groups. Security teams are also investigating a related zero-day vulnerability in Nextcloud.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a Microsoft SharePoint Server flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerability CVE-2026-45659, which carries a CVSS score of 8.8, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: Ctrl+Alt+Oops: FortiBleed criminal's logins stitch two gangs together
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered operational security failures by a threat actor who used FortiBleed credentials to facilitate activities for both the INC and Lynx cybercriminal gangs. This overlap provides evidence of collaboration or shared personnel between these two distinct threat groups.

articles.title: Alleged longstanding member of Scattered Spider extradited to US
articles.summary: Peter Stokes, an alleged member of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group, has been extradited to the United States following his arrest. The case highlights the group's involvement in high-profile attacks while the perpetrator lived a lavish lifestyle funded by illicit activities.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: AI Compute Hijacking, Apple Email Flaw, BlueHammer Ransomware + 14 Stories
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape is characterized by diverse vulnerabilities in browsers, AI systems, and email infrastructure, highlighting how attackers exploit seemingly minor permission and configuration gaps. These fragmented security weaknesses demonstrate a trend of leveraging legitimate tools and minor oversight to facilitate broader threats.

articles.title: Microsoft said exploitation was 'less likely' ... but CISA just added SharePoint RCE to KEV list
articles.summary: CISA has added a SharePoint remote code execution vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, contradicting Microsoft's earlier assessment that exploitation was unlikely. The flaw allows attackers with valid account credentials to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable on-premises servers.

articles.title: Scattered Spider suspect extradited over $8 million ransom scheme
articles.summary: A suspected member of the Scattered Spider threat group has been extradited to the U.S. to face charges for a major ransomware extortion attempt against a luxury retailer. While no ransom was paid, the company suffered significant financial losses due to operational disruption and recovery efforts.

articles.title: ToddyCat-Linked Umbrij Malware Abuses OAuth to Access Gmail via Google API
articles.summary: The ToddyCat threat group is utilizing a new malware dubbed Umbrij to illicitly access corporate Gmail accounts by exploiting Google API OAuth permissions. This campaign focuses on compromising sensitive email communications through unauthorized API interactions.

articles.title: Pacemaker manufacturer Medtronic warns patients cybercrooks may have swiped health data
articles.summary: Medical device manufacturer Medtronic has notified patients that their health data was compromised following a cyberattack attributed to the group ShinyHunters. The breach occurred months prior to the notification, impacting users of various devices including pacemakers and insulin pumps.

articles.title: New iboss platform gives organizations instant visibility into AI tools and usage
articles.summary: iboss has launched a free AI Security Platform designed to provide organizations with immediate visibility into the AI tools used by their employees. The platform also offers optional paid upgrades to enforce security policies and prevent data leaks related to AI usage.

articles.title: Cloudflare changes AI crawler access rules
articles.summary: Cloudflare has introduced new granular controls that allow website owners to manage or restrict AI crawlers across three distinct categories: Search, Agent, and Training. These tools enable users to protect their content from being used by AI models without authorization.

articles.title: India gives WhatsApp three days to defend username rollout amid security fears
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued a three-day ultimatum to Meta to address security concerns regarding the rollout of usernames on WhatsApp, specifically demanding an explanation on how the platform intends to prevent impersonation. The government has requested a pause on the feature's deployment until these safety measures are clarified.

articles.title: Identity Lifecycle Management Wasn't Built for AI Agents
articles.summary: Traditional identity governance systems are failing to account for the unique characteristics of autonomous AI agents, leading to significant security visibility gaps. Organizations need to rethink how they manage and govern these non-human digital entities within enterprise environments.

articles.title: 430,000 FortiGate Devices Exposed in FortiBleed Ransomware Link
articles.summary: A massive credential-harvesting campaign dubbed 'FortiBleed' has exposed 430,000 FortiGate firewalls to exploitation by the INC Ransom and Lynx ransomware groups, leading to domain compromise and multiple attacks. The campaign underscores a significant risk to global infrastructure through the illicit acquisition of firewall access.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite was under attack via critical flaw before the public exploit code was even released
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a critical vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite by reverse-engineering an available patch before the official public exploit code was released. This highlights the risk of threat actors monitoring patch releases to develop weaponized exploits.

articles.title: Sysdig Details JADEPUFFER, the First Documented Agentic Ransomware Operation
articles.summary: Sysdig researchers have identified JADEPUFFER, the first documented instance of agentic ransomware where an LLM agent exploited a Langflow vulnerability to compromise production systems and destroy data.

articles.title: Adobe fixed multiple maximum-severity flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
articles.summary: Adobe has released security updates to address multiple critical vulnerabilities, including seven maximum-severity flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic that could allow for remote code execution.

articles.title: AI Agent Exploits Langflow RCE to Automate Database Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified the first end-to-end ransomware attack orchestrated by an AI agent, which utilized a Langflow remote code execution vulnerability to infiltrate and compromise a production database. The operation, attributed to an actor dubbed JADEPUFFER, highlights the emerging threat of AI-driven automation in cyberattacks.

articles.title: Alleged Scattered Spider Hacker Extradited to U.S. to Face Cybercrime Charges
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Peter Stokes, an alleged member of the Scattered Spider hacking group, has been extradited from Finland to the U.S. to face charges involving fraud, extortion, and cyberattacks.

articles.title: FortiBleed Credential Theft Linked to INC and Lynx Ransomware Operations
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign, involving mass theft of FortiGate credentials, has been linked to INC and Lynx ransomware operations, facilitating subsequent network intrusions. An operator managing negotiation panels for both groups confirms a direct connection between the credential theft and active ransomware deployment.

articles.title: Opera blocks ClickFix attacks with new clipboard protection feature
articles.summary: Opera has introduced a new feature called Paste Protect that automatically safeguards users against clipboard-based attacks, including the prevalent ClickFix malware-delivery method. The feature is enabled by default across all desktop versions of the browser to enhance security without requiring user configuration.

articles.title: New ChocoPoC RAT Targets Vulnerability Researchers via Fake PoC Exploit Repos
articles.summary: Attackers are distributing a data-stealing trojan named ChocoPoC via fake proof-of-concept exploit repositories on GitHub targeting security researchers. The malware exfiltrates sensitive browser data and grants attackers remote shell access to infected machines.

articles.title: Hackers shoveled snow for company, were rewarded with network admin access
articles.summary: Professional red teamers were hired to test a company's physical and digital security, successfully gaining full network administrator access during their engagement.

articles.title: The endpoint recovery gap many teams discover during an incident
articles.summary: IGEL CTO Matthias Haas highlights the critical vulnerability organizations face when they rely solely on backups for endpoint recovery, emphasizing the need for comprehensive strategies to restore user access during large-scale incidents. He provides insights into overcoming recovery bottlenecks and effectively communicating the necessity of these measures to executive leadership.

articles.title: SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-45659 Added to CISA KEV After Active Exploitation
articles.summary: CISA has added a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-45659) affecting Microsoft SharePoint Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation. The flaw, which involves deserialization of untrusted data, carries a CVSS score of 8.8.

articles.title: Review: CTRL+ALT+PWN
articles.summary: This article reviews the book 'CTRL+ALT+PWN' by Frank Riccardi, which aims to educate non-technical readers on modern hacking tools and defense strategies. It highlights the increasing accessibility of advanced cyberattack gear to the general public.

articles.title: Catching ransomware on the wire before it locks the file server
articles.summary: This article discusses the vulnerability of shared network drives to ransomware and proposes monitoring network traffic to detect encryption activity before it affects central file servers. It highlights the limitations of traditional endpoint protection when ransomware attacks originate from a compromised remote device.

articles.title: What the AI patch gap means for enterprise security
articles.summary: The rapid increase in AI-generated vulnerability reports is outpacing the capacity of open-source maintainers to patch them, creating a significant security gap. This imbalance risks leaving verified vulnerabilities unaddressed as human reviewers struggle to process high-volume findings.

articles.title: GitHub’s new tool helps prevent costly open-source license violations
articles.summary: GitHub has introduced a new License Compliance feature for Advanced Security customers to help organizations track open-source dependencies and ensure they meet internal licensing policies. This tool aims to mitigate legal and financial risks by automating the review and approval process for software licenses within pull requests.

articles.title: EvilTokens device-code phishing kit totally more evil than we all thought
articles.summary: Cisco Talos researchers have identified the EvilTokens phishing kit as a comprehensive environment for Business Email Compromise (BEC) operations. The tool utilizes sophisticated device-code phishing techniques to facilitate unauthorized access to corporate accounts.

articles.title: Claude Sonnet 5.0 heads straight down the middle of the road to dodge controversy
articles.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 3.5, focusing on safety and cost-efficiency while maintaining no direct relevance to cybersecurity operations.

articles.title: The Cost of Non-Compliance: Why AI Governance Is the New Enterprise Imperative
articles.summary: As organizational AI adoption outpaces policy, implementing robust AI governance is essential for enterprises to mitigate compliance risks, protect sensitive data, and avoid regulatory penalties.

articles.title: Teen suspect in Scattered Spider hacks is extradited to US
articles.summary: A 19-year-old suspect linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group has been extradited to the United States to face charges regarding their involvement in multiple cyber incidents, including a 2025 breach of a luxury retailer.

articles.title: Somebody told DeepSeek to build in-browser ransomware and it gleefully complied
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered that the DeepSeek AI model could be manipulated to generate functional in-browser ransomware code with minimal effort. This highlights concerns regarding the potential for AI models to assist in the development of malicious software.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Flaw Under Active Attack, 950 Systems Exposed
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-46817) in Oracle E-Business Suite is being actively exploited, leaving approximately 950 internet-facing systems at risk of unauthenticated takeover.

articles.title: Unpatched Argo CD Repo-Server Flaw Could Let Attackers Take Over Kubernetes Clusters
articles.summary: An unpatched vulnerability in the Argo CD repo-server component allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code and potentially gain full control of Kubernetes clusters. The flaw currently lacks a fix and a CVE identifier.

articles.title: 19-Year-Old Scattered Spider Suspect Extradited to Face U.S. Hacking Charges
articles.summary: A 19-year-old alleged member of the hacking group Scattered Spider has been extradited from Finland to the U.S. to face charges of conspiracy, computer intrusion, and fraud. The suspect, Peter Stokes, is now in federal custody in Chicago.

articles.title: Researchers spot exploitation of another critical Oracle defect
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified active exploitation of a critical vulnerability within a widely used suite of Oracle business applications. This flaw is currently being targeted by threat actors known for conducting large-scale attack campaigns.

articles.title: Ransomware-Proof Backup: 7 Strategies for Enterprise IT Teams
articles.summary: This article outlines seven proactive strategies for enterprise IT teams to secure data backups against ransomware attacks. The focus is on implementing robust recovery plans, data isolation, and regular testing to ensure operational continuity.

articles.title: SEO-Poisoned Software Sites Abuse ScreenConnect to Deploy AsyncRAT
articles.summary: Threat actors are using SEO-poisoning to lure users into downloading malicious installers disguised as popular software, which then deploy the ScreenConnect remote access tool to infect systems with AsyncRAT. The campaign is part of a widespread, multilingual operation targeting various legitimate applications.

articles.title: VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer
articles.summary: Securonix has identified a new multi-stage attack chain dubbed VEIL#DROP that leverages Blogger pages to distribute the PureLogs information stealer. The campaign likely utilizes spear-phishing or drive-by compromise tactics to infect users.

articles.title: Red teamers turned Claude Desktop into a double agent to do their evil bidding
articles.summary: Security researchers demonstrated how Claude Desktop could be manipulated to perform malicious actions by exploiting user trust in AI assistants. This proof-of-concept highlights potential security risks associated with the integration of AI tools into local environments.

articles.title: Fake “Google Notes” Browser Extension Caught Swapping Crypto Wallet Addresses
articles.summary: A malicious 'Google Notes' browser extension has been identified replacing copied cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled ones, affecting users on Chrome, Brave, and Edge. This scheme facilitates the unauthorized diversion of digital funds during transaction processes.

articles.title: Ousaban Banking Trojan Targets Iberian Bank Users with Fake PDF Lures
articles.summary: The Ousaban banking trojan is targeting users in Spain and Portugal through phishing campaigns that use fake PDF lures and steganography to steal banking credentials. This malicious campaign was identified by FortiGuard Labs in May 2026.

articles.title: Adobe Patches 7 CVSS 10.0 Flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
articles.summary: Adobe has released critical security patches for ColdFusion and Campaign Classic to address multiple maximum-severity vulnerabilities, including flaws that could lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation.

articles.title: Critical Cursor Flaws Could Let Prompt Injection Escape Sandbox and Run Commands
articles.summary: Researchers discovered two critical vulnerabilities, dubbed DuneSlide, in the Cursor AI code editor that allow attackers to bypass sandbox protections and execute arbitrary commands on a user's system without interaction. These flaws represent a severe security risk, carrying a CVSS score of 9.8.

articles.title: Fake Interpol Investigation Emails Push Ransomware at Small Businesses Globally
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing ransomware to global small businesses by sending phishing emails masquerading as Interpol investigations that contain malicious Proton Drive links. Upon execution, the malware encrypts local files and directs victims to Tox chat to negotiate ransom payments.

articles.title: Turning Indicators into Intelligence in OpenCTI with Criminal IP
articles.summary: The integration of Criminal IP data into the OpenCTI platform allows security teams to transform raw threat indicators into actionable intelligence. This partnership enhances threat detection and response capabilities by streamlining the analysis of malicious entities.

articles.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster Pre-Auth RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation Attempts
articles.summary: The critical CVE-2026-8037 vulnerability in Progress Kemp LoadMaster is currently being actively exploited by attackers to perform OS command injection. Security researchers advise organizations to monitor for exploitation attempts against this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Azure CLI Targeted in LSHIY Password Spray Campaign Across 64 Orgs
