articles.summary: An automated password spray campaign dubbed LSHIY has targeted Microsoft Azure CLI environments, resulting in 81 million login attempts and 78 compromised accounts across 64 organizations. Researchers at Huntress discovered the campaign has been active since June 2026.

articles.title: U.S. lifting export control restrictions on Anthropic’s Mythos, Fable
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department has agreed to lift export control restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable AI models, allowing them to be released publicly with enhanced guardrails and classifiers.

articles.title: US lifts export controls on Anthropic’s frontier cybersecurity AI models
articles.summary: The U.S. government has eased export restrictions on specific frontier cybersecurity AI models developed by Anthropic following new collaborative agreements. This move reflects updated regulatory oversight regarding the international distribution of advanced security-focused artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Japanese insurer, brewer, manufacturer and telecom disclose cyber breaches
articles.summary: Several major Japanese corporations, including Aflac's Tokyo branch and Sapporo, have publicly disclosed data breaches. These incidents highlight a significant wave of security compromises across diverse sectors in Japan.

articles.title: AI-Generated Browser Ransomware Abuses Chromium API on Windows and Android
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new browser-based ransomware strain generated by DeepSeek that exploits Chromium APIs to target both Windows and Android platforms. This marks a concerning milestone as the first documented instance of a frontier AI model facilitating the creation of a functional, cross-platform malicious attack.

articles.title: Mitigating Attacks Before They Impact Infrastructure: Link11 provides next generation network DDoS protection
articles.summary: Link11 has introduced a next-generation network DDoS protection solution designed to block cyberattacks before they can affect critical infrastructure. This announcement highlights a proactive approach to mitigating large-scale volumetric threats.

articles.title: Netzilo adds runtime governance for AI agents across major platforms
articles.summary: Netzilo has expanded its security platform to provide runtime governance and enforcement for AI agents deployed across various cloud and enterprise environments. The update aims to help security teams monitor and manage the growing risks associated with moving AI agents into production.

articles.title: Dawnguard launches platform to automate secure cloud architecture
articles.summary: Dawnguard has officially launched its cloud security architecture automation platform and secured $3.3 million in additional pre-seed funding. The platform is designed to assist organizations in building and maintaining secure cloud-native environments from initial development through production.

articles.title: 2026 Cybersecurity Assessment: The Gap Between Awareness and Resilience
articles.summary: The 2026 Bitdefender Cybersecurity Assessment reveals a significant disconnect between increased organizational awareness of cyber threats and the practical ability to achieve operational resilience. Survey results from 1,200 professionals highlight growing contradictions in how businesses manage and mitigate security risks.

articles.title: Intruder offers Free security plan for lean IT and security teams
articles.summary: Intruder has introduced a free vulnerability management and cloud security plan to assist lean IT and DevOps teams in smaller organizations with their security posture. This offering aims to bridge the resource gap that often leaves mid-sized businesses vulnerable to cyber threats.

articles.title: CISA Warns BlueHammer Flaw Is Now Exploited in Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: CISA has confirmed that the BlueHammer vulnerability (CVE-2026-33825) is being actively exploited in the wild to gain SYSTEM privileges via Microsoft Defender for ransomware attacks.

articles.title: Microsoft Accelerates Post-Quantum Cryptography Shift to 2029
articles.summary: Microsoft is accelerating its transition to post-quantum cryptography to 2029 due to rapid advancements in quantum computing that threaten current encryption standards. The move aims to proactively address the shifting risk landscape posed by future quantum-based decryption capabilities.

articles.title: RustDuck: The Botnet That’s Still Small but Engineering Like It Plans to Grow
articles.summary: RustDuck is an emerging DDoS botnet that leverages the Rust programming language, advanced anti-analysis techniques, and known IoT vulnerabilities to hijack various devices for large-scale attacks. Researchers are monitoring its development as it expands its operational capabilities.

articles.title: The ARToken phishing panel targets Microsoft 365 accounts
articles.summary: The ARToken phishing operation is actively targeting Microsoft 365 accounts by sending deceptive invoice-related emails to accounts-payable staff. These highly targeted social engineering lures impersonate legitimate vendors to compromise corporate financial information.

articles.title: This phishing kit looks more like BEC-as-a-service
articles.summary: Cisco Talos research highlights the evolution of phishing-as-a-service platforms, specifically focusing on the ARToken kit and its operational similarities to Business Email Compromise (BEC) tactics. The report underscores how these kits are becoming increasingly sophisticated to facilitate large-scale credential harvesting.

articles.title: Claude Sonnet 5 includes safeguards against dangerous cyber use
articles.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 5, which features enhanced autonomous capabilities and improved reasoning while incorporating updated safety measures to prevent misuse for cyberattacks.

articles.title: GuardFall Flaw Hits 10 of 11 Popular Open-Source AI Agents
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a universal shell injection vulnerability called GuardFall affecting 10 out of 11 popular open-source AI agents, enabling attackers to bypass security filters. The flaw exposes these AI tools to potential unauthorized command execution.

articles.title: Phantom Squatting Uses AI-Hallucinated Domains for Phishing and Malware
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting AI-generated hallucinations by registering non-existent domains suggested by large language models to host phishing and malware campaigns. This emerging technique, known as phantom squatting, leverages the trust users place in AI-provided resources.

articles.title: Anthropic Restores Claude Fable 5 After U.S. Lifts Jailbreak-Linked Export Controls
articles.summary: Anthropic has restored access to its Claude Fable 5 model worldwide following the U.S. Commerce Department's decision to lift export controls that were originally imposed due to jailbreak-related security concerns.

articles.title: What a financial planner taught me about cybersecurity
articles.summary: A cybersecurity speaker observes that financial professionals are often overwhelmed and fearful when confronted with the realities of cyber threats. The article highlights the importance of effective security awareness training for high-stakes industries.

articles.title: Nika: Open-source code analysis tool
articles.summary: PhonePe has released Nika, an open-source code analysis tool designed to identify complex security vulnerabilities in Java microservices by performing multi-file path analysis. This approach overcomes the limitations of single-file scanners by tracking data flows across different layers of an application.

articles.title: Azure CLI Password Spray Hits at Least 78 Microsoft Accounts in 81M+ Attempts
articles.summary: An ongoing automated password spray attack targeting Microsoft's Azure CLI has successfully compromised at least 78 accounts after over 81 million attempts. The malicious activity has been traced to a specific IPv6 address range operated by infrastructure provider LSHIY LLC.

articles.title: Researcher Analyzes 3,000 Live ClickFix Payloads, Exposing API-Driven Malware Delivery
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered that ClickFix campaigns are now utilizing API-driven infrastructure to dynamically serve unique malware payloads, while also introducing new techniques to evade Windows script scanning.

articles.title: This supercomputer encrypts your data even while it’s running it
articles.summary: A new supercomputer technology has been developed to maintain data encryption while it is actively being processed in memory, closing a critical security gap where data is traditionally exposed. This advancement mitigates risks associated with memory-scraping attacks and unauthorized access during computation.

articles.title: AI-generated code risks reach security, legal, and compliance teams
articles.summary: A Flux survey reveals that nearly half of engineering organizations are running AI-generated code in production, raising concerns regarding security, legal, and compliance risks. Most companies have adopted AI in development workflows, highlighting a broad shift in software engineering practices despite potential security oversight gaps.

articles.title: Microsoft wants to stop unwanted bots from entering Teams meetings
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a new admin policy for Teams that enhances visibility and control over external bots, allowing administrators to implement specific safeguards for meeting access. This change aims to replace the legacy CAPTCHA-based verification with more deliberate, policy-driven bot management.

articles.title: Getting boards to fund ERM means speaking their currency
articles.summary: Greg Young explains that cybersecurity leaders can secure funding for Enterprise Risk Management by framing it in terms of business value and risk intelligence rather than mere governance. The strategy emphasizes aligning security initiatives with board-level decision-making processes.

articles.title: Citrix Patches Six NetScaler Flaws Allowing File Read and Denial-of-Service
articles.summary: Citrix has released security updates to patch six vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that could allow attackers to perform arbitrary file reads or cause denial-of-service conditions.

articles.title: Phantom Squatting: AI-Hallucinated Domains as a Software Supply Chain Vector
articles.summary: Attackers are leveraging LLM-generated hallucinated domains to conduct phantom squatting attacks, creating new risks for software supply chain security. This technique exploits the tendency of AI models to recommend non-existent but plausible-looking package dependencies that adversaries can then register.

articles.title: XSS.is, The Forum That Ran the Ransomware Supply Chain Is Down. The Market Isn’t
articles.summary: French and Ukrainian law enforcement authorities arrested the alleged administrator of XSS.is and seized the influential Russian-language cybercrime forum. Despite the takedown, experts indicate the broader cybercriminal market remains active.

articles.title: Proton’s pitch for Lumo 2.0: Frontier AI without the data grab
articles.summary: Proton has launched Lumo 2.0, a privacy-focused AI assistant that utilizes zero-access encryption to provide advanced multimodal capabilities and enterprise features without compromising user data.

articles.title: Citrix patches a new NetScaler flaw with echoes of CitrixBleed
articles.summary: Citrix has released patches for six vulnerabilities in NetScaler, including a high-severity flaw that shares concerning similarities with the previously exploited CitrixBleed vulnerability.

articles.title: Trump budget boss Russell Vought open to re-staffing CISA
articles.summary: Potential plans to restore 600 staff positions at CISA, which were previously reduced under the Trump administration, are currently being discussed by officials. This move suggests a potential shift in federal cybersecurity workforce policy.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SimpleHelp flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in SimpleHelp (CVE-2026-48558) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw affects versions 5.5.15 and earlier and holds a CVSS score of 10.0.

articles.title: Infosec professionals sour on automated pentesting tools
articles.summary: Recent data indicates a significant decline in industry confidence toward fully autonomous penetration testing tools among security professionals. The drop from 29% to 9% suggests a growing skepticism regarding the effectiveness or reliability of complete automation in security assessments.

articles.title: CIA chief highlights major shifts in agency’s tech approach
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe emphasized the strategic importance of artificial intelligence, comparing its potential impact and power to digital nuclear weapons. This highlights the agency's shifting priority toward integrating advanced AI capabilities into their intelligence framework.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns Poisoned MCP Tool Descriptions Can Make AI Agents Leak Data
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered a vulnerability where malicious, poisoned tool descriptions can manipulate AI agents into exfiltrating sensitive company data without triggering security alerts. The exploit functions by tricking the agent into performing unauthorized actions that appear legitimate, bypassing standard security oversight.

articles.title: RustDuck Botnet Rebuilds in Rust to Hijack Routers and Servers for DDoS
articles.summary: The RustDuck botnet is utilizing the Rust programming language to rapidly evolve its infrastructure, targeting IoT devices and servers for large-scale DDoS attacks. Researchers highlight the botnet's concerning growth rate and frequent tactical updates.

articles.title: New EvilTokens Attack Exposes Browser Visibility Gap in Enterprise SOCs
articles.summary: The EvilTokens phishing attack exploits a visibility gap by delaying takeover indicators until browser execution, complicating threat detection for enterprise SOC teams. Organizations must enhance monitoring to validate these threats and mitigate account compromise risks.

articles.title: Huntress CEO says threat hunter used 'poor judgment' in alerting ransomware crim about law enforcement probe
articles.summary: The CEO of Huntress acknowledged that a threat hunter demonstrated poor judgment by notifying a ransomware operator about an ongoing law enforcement investigation. This incident has raised concerns regarding insider threats and the ethical boundaries of cybersecurity professional conduct.

articles.title: Modern Enterprises: How to Evaluate the Security and Compliance of Office Software
articles.summary: This article provides a framework for businesses to evaluate office software based on critical security standards like ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance. It focuses on best practices for ensuring data protection and secure document workflows.

articles.title: House passes kids’ online safety bill, but Senate approval unlikely
articles.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed the KIDS Act with a bipartisan majority, although the bill faces significant hurdles in the Senate. This legislation aims to enhance online protections for children, though its future enactment remains uncertain.

articles.title: Hackers Steal Data of 4.38 Million Aflac Japan Customers
articles.summary: Hackers exfiltrated the personal data of 4.38 million Aflac Japan customers and agents after maintaining unauthorized access to company systems for a 10-day period in June.

articles.title: Langflow RCE Exploited to Deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical unauthenticated RCE vulnerability, CVE-2026-33017, in Langflow to deploy Monero cryptocurrency miners on exposed AI application endpoints. This campaign highlights the growing targeting of AI infrastructure by malicious actors.

articles.title: Silent Swap Crypto Clipper Uses Fake Google Notes Extension to Replace Wallet Addresses
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a campaign called Silent Swap that uses malicious browser extensions to steal cryptocurrency by replacing user wallet addresses during transactions. The malware is distributed via unsigned installers developed in .NET and Golang.

articles.title: DHS to unveil replacement council for critical infrastructure cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Department of Homeland Security is launching a new council to facilitate cybersecurity information sharing between the government and critical infrastructure sectors. This initiative serves as a replacement for a previously disbanded program aimed at strengthening operational resilience.

articles.title: Hackers Use Fake FIFA World Cup 2026 T-Shirt Offers to Spread Voidrift Malware
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing Voidrift malware via phishing emails that leverage fake FIFA World Cup 2026 merchandise offers. The campaign utilizes trusted branding and websites to evade security detection mechanisms.

articles.title: NDSS Symposium Heads to Seoul in 2027 to Expand Global Cybersecurity Collaboration
articles.summary: The NDSS Symposium has announced it will host its 2027 conference in Seoul to foster international cooperation and knowledge exchange in the cybersecurity field.

articles.title: Reflectiz to Host Webinar, Joined by Taboola, on Securing Third-Party Marketing in the AI Era
articles.summary: Reflectiz and Taboola are co-hosting a webinar focused on strategies for securing third-party marketing applications within the context of artificial intelligence. The event aims to address the growing security challenges associated with digital marketing integrations.

articles.title: GuardFall Exposes Open-Source AI Coding Agents to Decades-Old Shell Injection Risks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered 'GuardFall,' a vulnerability affecting most open-source AI coding agents that allows attackers to bypass security filters using legacy shell injection techniques. The flaw enables malicious commands to be executed despite the presence of safety checks.

articles.title: Aikido Security acquires Root to expand backported fixes for open source vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Aikido Security has acquired Root to integrate backported fixes for open source vulnerabilities and improve protection against supply chain attacks. This move aims to help developers secure their software dependencies more effectively.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Payments flaw under attack (CVE-2026-46817)
articles.summary: Threat intelligence firm Defused reported active in-the-wild exploitation of a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-46817) in the Oracle E-Business Suite Payments module. The attacks were detected approximately six weeks after the release of the official security patch.

articles.title: Cequence Platform 9.0 uses AI to simplify API security and compliance
articles.summary: Cequence Security has released Platform 9.0, an AI-native update featuring a new AI Assistant, automated compliance frameworks, and an enhanced API security engine for large-scale enterprise environments.

articles.title: An intelligence budget 'super user' job is now in the hands of Russ Vought
articles.summary: Russell Vought has taken direct control over the budget oversight of U.S. intelligence agencies following the resignation of official Amaryllis Fox Kennedy. This shift centralizes financial supervision of intelligence operations under the Office of Management and Budget director.

articles.title: 282 iOS AI Apps Leak API Keys and Open AI Proxy Access in Network Traffic Study
articles.summary: A study of 444 iOS AI apps revealed that 282 exposed sensitive API keys and backend credentials in plaintext, allowing unauthorized users to exploit developer accounts. This massive security oversight affects approximately two-thirds of the tested applications.

articles.title: Jamf enables AI Governance and shadow AI detection on Mac
articles.summary: Jamf has introduced AI Governance capabilities for Mac to help IT and security teams detect unsanctioned AI tools and enforce usage policies across their device fleets. The new feature provides visibility into AI application usage to assist with security audits and compliance management.

articles.title: Digi International’s DANI automates network diagnostics and device management
articles.summary: Digi International has launched DANI, an AI-powered network operations agent integrated into its Digi Remote Manager platform to streamline network diagnostics, issue identification, and remediation. The tool leverages a conversational interface to provide real-time monitoring and actionable insights for network operators.

articles.title: OpenMatter Network brings verifiable trust to AI governance
articles.summary: OpenMatter Network has launched a cryptographically verifiable platform designed to secure AI governance and data collaboration by replacing traditional trust-based models with verifiable proof. This initiative aims to address the security challenges posed by autonomous AI agents operating across distributed enterprise environments.

articles.title: AppViewX Launches Global Partner Program Amid Rising Demand for Machine and Agent Identity Security
articles.summary: AppViewX has introduced a new global partner program to address the increasing market demand for advanced machine and agent identity security solutions.

articles.title: OpenMatter Network Introduces Verifiable Trust Layer for Secure Collaboration and AI Agents
articles.summary: OpenMatter Network has launched a new verifiable trust layer designed to secure collaborative environments and support the integration of AI agents. The platform aims to enhance security protocols for distributed digital interactions.

articles.title: Apple Fixes WebKit Flaws in iOS and macOS, With Help From AI Tools
articles.summary: Apple has released security updates for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and Safari to patch multiple WebKit vulnerabilities. Notably, four of these flaws were identified using AI-driven tools like Claude and Codex.

articles.title: What the Numbers Say About FIFA 2026 Cyber Risk
articles.summary: Check Point Research reports that threat actors established sophisticated fraud infrastructure targeting the FIFA World Cup 2026 months in advance, operating across multiple sectors and languages. The findings highlight the significant pre-planned cyber threat landscape surrounding the global event.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558 to Deploy TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-48558, in SimpleHelp to deploy the TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer malware families.

articles.title: WhatsApp Usernames Will Let You Chat Without Sharing Your Phone Number
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing a username feature that allows users to communicate without exposing their phone numbers, enhancing privacy and user identity management. This update aims to reduce unauthorized contact and potential harassment by decoupling accounts from phone numbers.

articles.title: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited to deliver mighty Djinn Stealer (CVE-2026-48558)
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a patched authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-48558) in SimpleHelp RMM software to deploy a cross-platform information-stealing malware known as Djinn Stealer.

articles.title: AirDrop and Quick Share Flaws Let Nearby Attackers Trigger Crashes and Bypass Checks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered six security vulnerabilities in Apple's AirDrop and Android's Quick Share that allow nearby attackers to crash services or bypass security checks without user interaction. These flaws exploit wireless proximity to target devices configured to accept files from anyone.

articles.title: Attackers actively exploit the Oracle E-Business Suite flaw CVE-2026-46817
articles.summary: Oracle E-Business Suite is currently under active exploitation due to a critical remote code execution vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-46817. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to fully compromise Oracle Payments systems.

articles.title: How ransomware syndicates weaponize corporate-style organization
articles.summary: Modern ransomware groups are increasingly adopting corporate operational structures, utilizing outsourced labor and tiered pricing models to function like large, professionalized organizations. This transition reflects a shift in cybercriminal strategy toward highly organized, business-like enterprise operations.

articles.title: New BioShocking Attack Tricks AI Browsers Into Leaking User Credentials
articles.summary: Security researchers at LayerX discovered 'BioShocking,' a technique that exploits AI browsers and assistants by manipulating them into exfiltrating user credentials. The vulnerability affects several major platforms, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude extensions.

articles.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster Flaw Could Let Attackers Run Root Commands Pre-Auth
articles.summary: A critical pre-authentication remote command execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-8037, affects Progress Kemp LoadMaster appliances with the API enabled. Users are urged to apply the available security patch immediately to prevent unauthorized root access.

articles.title: Apple Patches 30+ iOS, macOS, Safari Flaws, Including AI-Discovered WebKit Bugs
articles.summary: Apple has issued security updates for iOS, macOS, and Safari to remediate over 30 vulnerabilities, including four WebKit flaws identified through the use of AI tools.

articles.title: Microsoft builds a bouncer to keep bots out of Teams meetings
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a new authentication mechanism for Microsoft Teams that allows independent software vendors to verify their bots, ensuring legitimate automated tools can access meetings while blocking unauthorized ones.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Flaw CVE-2026-46817 Actively Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary: A critical privilege management and authentication flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite (CVE-2026-46817) is being actively exploited in the wild, posing a severe risk of full system takeover.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 30, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security provides a curated list of cybersecurity job openings for June 30, 2026, featuring roles in AI offensive security and enterprise authentication.

articles.title: India’s central bank mandated use of .bank domains to enhance trust – but its registry leaked sensitive info
articles.summary: India's central bank mandate to use .bank domains for security was undermined by an open API that exposed sensitive information, facilitating potential impersonation attacks. The incident highlights a critical failure in the implementation of security-focused infrastructure.

articles.title: Security researchers tricked LLMs into giving them cocaine recipes by abusing role models for prompt injection
articles.summary: Security researchers successfully bypassed LLM safety guardrails using prompt injection techniques that leverage role-play scenarios to elicit restricted information. This highlights ongoing challenges in securing AI models against manipulative inputs.

articles.title: WhatsApp Usernames Are Coming. You Can Reserve Yours Right Now
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing a new username feature that allows users to communicate without sharing personal phone numbers. The feature is scheduled for release later this year, with a reservation period currently open for users.

articles.title: Four years into Ukraine invasion, Russia turns influence-ops back to US and Europe
articles.summary: Russia has resumed focused influence operations targeting the United States and Europe, four years into the ongoing invasion of Ukraine. These campaigns aim to sway public opinion and leverage geopolitical tensions within Western nations.

articles.title: U.S. Targets Russian Cyber Spies With $10M Bounty Over Messaging App Attacks
articles.summary: The U.S. government is offering a $10 million reward for information leading to the identification of Russian hackers from groups UNC5792 and UNC4221 who target the Signal and WhatsApp accounts of officials and journalists.
